Maon
MAY-on
proper noun
Hebrew Ma’on, “a dwelling” or “habitation,” a town in the hill country of Judah with a wilderness about it.

📖 Biblical Definition

Maon was a town in the hill country of Judah (Josh 15:55), set on the edge of a wilderness that bore its name, in the dry pasture-land south of Hebron. It was in the wilderness of Maon that David hid from Saul, and there Saul nearly took him: David was on one side of the mountain and Saul on the other, and Saul had compassed David and his men round about, when a messenger came that the Philistines had invaded the land, and Saul was forced to turn away — so that the place was called the rock of divisions (1Sa 23:24–28). In Maon also dwelt Nabal, a man very great in flocks but churlish and evil in his doings, whose possessions were in nearby Carmel (1Sa 25:2). When Nabal returned David’s kindness with insult, David purposed vengeance, but the wise and gracious Abigail met him with her gift and her counsel, and turned away his wrath; and the LORD Himself smote Nabal that he died (1Sa 25). Maon thus stands as a place of David’s testing in the wilderness years, where the LORD delivered him from Saul by a sudden providence and kept him from avenging himself by the timely wisdom of a godly woman. It witnesses the watchful care of God over His anointed in the days of his affliction.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the hill country of Judah with a wilderness about it, where David hid from Saul and Nabal dwelt.

expand to see more

MAON, a town in the hill country of Judah south of Hebron.

A wilderness bore its name in the dry pasture-land about it.

There David hid from Saul, who was turned away by a Philistine raid (1Sa 23:25–28).

There dwelt Nabal, churlish and rich, whose flocks were in Carmel (1Sa 25:2).

Abigail of this region turned away David’s wrath from blood (1Sa 25).

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 15:55 — "Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah,"

1Sa 23:24 — "And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon."

1Sa 23:25 — "Saul also and his men went to seek him. And they told David: wherefore he came down into a rock, and abode in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon."

1Sa 25:2 — "And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is the watchful providence of God over His servant in affliction.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the providence that twice delivered David at Maon. When Saul had all but closed his net, a Philistine raid drew him away at the very hour of David’s peril; and when David himself was about to sin in vengeance against Nabal, God sent Abigail to stay his hand. The LORD watches over His own, delivering them both from their enemies and from their own rash anger.

Maon also sets the churlish Nabal beside the prudent Abigail, the fool who despised David against the wise woman who honoured the LORD’s anointed. Nabal’s name means “fool,” and his end proved it; vengeance belonged to God, who smote him without David lifting a hand. The believer learns at Maon to leave his cause with the Lord rather than avenge himself.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “a dwelling” or “habitation,” fitting a settled town amid the wilderness pastures.

expand to see more

Maon — Hebrew Ma’on, “a dwelling” or “habitation.”

The same word is used of God as the dwelling-place of His people (Ps 90:1).

A wilderness south of Hebron bore the town’s name.

It lay near Carmel of Judah, where Nabal sheared his sheep.

The dwelling-town became a place of David’s wilderness testing.

Usage

"Like David at Maon, the servant of God is delivered by providence both from his enemies and from his own wrath."

"Maon teaches the believer to leave vengeance with the LORD, who smote Nabal without David’s hand."

"The rock of divisions at Maon witnesses God’s timely care over His afflicted anointed."
